To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the task was feasible, as the participants were able to find a significant amount of correct relations; 2) there are no significant differences in the results obtained by the different systems, and 3) the best performing system was the one that used the largest number of features, and the one that used a large amount of lexical resources.

(1) the structural similarity measure is not suitable for evaluating the quality of taxonomies; (2) the quality of taxonomic relations can be assessed manually, and (3) the quality of the relations is not related to their frequency in the gold standard.

the best performing systems achieved a structural similarity with the gold standard of about 0.5, and that the structural similarity is highly correlated with the manual assessment of the quality of the extracted relations.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the task is very hard and that the participating systems did not achieve good results.
the participating systems performed well on structural measures but not so well on finding novel relations.
the task is still open to further improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participating systems performed well in the task of finding hypernym-hyposynm relations between given terms, but they performed poorly in finding the correct taxonomy for a given set of terms.
the results show that the state of the art is not mature enough for automatic taxonomy extraction.
the results of the shared task are encouraging and that there is room for improvements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural measures alone are not sufficient to evaluate the performance of the systems and that the manual quality assessment of the extracted relations is a crucial part of the evaluation.
, while automatic methods are able to identify many of the hypernyms in the gold standard, there is a significant number of novel relations that are missed.
the structural measures are very sensitive to the quality of the gold standard and should not be used as the only evaluation metric.
